sections.title: What you bring, and what lighthouse checks
text: lighthouse installs none of these. lighthouse init checks every tool that the packs it installs need. When one is missing, it reports "missing dependency: <tool> (needed by: …)" and goes on. It does not check Claude Code.
A tool per language matters only with the pack for that language, which init proposes when it recognises your repository. codex is optional: it runs the reviews by another model family.

sections.title: Rules
text: init writes a managed block into AGENTS.md: the rules every lighthouse repo shares, a part per pack. Your own text in the file stays as it is.
CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md with the line @AGENTS.md, so Claude Code reads the same rules as Codex and OpenCode. init adds that line only when neither file exists yet; otherwise you add it yourself.

sections.title: Config
text: lighthouse.toml, in the root of your repo, holds the settings of your project, such as the language of its issues and pull requests and the test command. That command runs on your workstation after every commit; CI runs on GitHub. init adds the keys that are missing and leaves the rest as it is.
.lighthouse/ holds the manifest of what init installed and at which version, the headings the skills write and read, and the helper code of the hooks and skills.
One file lands outside your repo: ~/.config/lighthouse/host.toml on your workstation. init offers it only on a machine with Tailscale.
